focus: TitanValue.cs StatPart_TitanTraits: mode detection (card/trade/wealth), base value before material part, ExplanationPart's BaseBeforeThisPart recomputation (recursion, other mods' parts), floor, threading of TradeSession/HidingFor, WealthWatcher pawn wealth path
diffSource: since build 49 (2026-10-07T05:09:27Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: TradeSession.Active stays true for the rest of the game after the first trade, so colony wealth takes the Trade branch
findings.detail: TradeSession.Active is `trader != null`, and only TradeSession.Close() clears it. Nothing in vanilla or the fetched mod corpus calls Close() (Dialog_Trade.Close does not). After the first trade, ModeFor returns Mode.Trade for every main-thread MarketValue read. That includes WealthWatcher.ForceRecount's `item.MarketValue` over player pawns (WealthWatcher.cs:143), so colony wealth and raid points leave hidden traits out and add the mystery bonus, the opposite of the documented design. In ModeFor (Source/TitanValue.cs:83), also require the trade dialog to be open, e.g. `TradeSession.Active && Find.WindowStack.IsOpen<Dialog_Trade>()`. Trade prices are still covered because Tradeable.InitPriceDataIfNeeded reads MarketValue lazily while the dialog is drawing (Tradeable.cs:250-259).

findings.title: Mystery bonus also raises the price the player pays when buying a titan from a trader
findings.detail: In Trade mode, mystery is added for any pawn with a hidden trait, whichever side owns it. That includes the trader's own stock (and gift-mode goodwill). If the bonus is only meant for selling, check whether the pawn belongs to the player before adding it. This is a design reading, not a defect.

findings.title: An info card opened from the trade dialog shows a lower market value than the trade price
findings.detail: ModeFor checks HidingFor before TradeSession, so the card of a titan with hidden traits, opened during a trade, uses Card mode and leaves out the mystery bonus the trade row includes. The two numbers will differ.

findings.title: BaseBeforeThisPart runs every part if another mod removes this part from MarketValue.parts
findings.detail: The loop stops when it reaches `this`. If the part has been removed or replaced, it runs the whole list, material part included, and TitanValueUtility.BaseValue returns a value with the material in it. This can't happen with the current startup code; it only matters if another mod rebuilds the parts list.
